title: The tail of zlib is Adler-32 for decompressing data
summary: The last four bytes of a zlib stream store the Adler-32 of the uncompressed data in big-endian order.
detail: Also using DEFLATE, gzip outer layer uses CRC32 and ISIZE, bare DEFLATE does not have the tail of zlib.
boundary: Only by first determining the outer package can the last four bytes be interpreted; the presence of common header bytes alone cannot prove that the file is complete.
relevance: Explain the phenomenon that the compressed content can be decrypted but checking the tail using CRC32 continues to fail.
